lead.headline: Nvidia's CEO Resigns and Its Stock Slides About 10%, Oil Rebounds Toward $94 and Russia-Ukraine Talks End Without a Deal, While Fed Hike Bets Stay Alive
lead.deck: Wednesday's tech rally erased the Nasdaq's post-election losses, but Thursday opens with futures lower; California gas has fallen to about $5.63 and Los Angeles rents are soft.

board_note: Figures as of Nov. 11-12 unless noted (mortgage Nov. 5, gold Nov. 9); S&P level not published in sources read; sources in each story.

stories.headline: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Resigns and the Stock Sinks About 10%; CFO Colette Kress Becomes Interim CEO Five Days Before Earnings
stories.deck: The board accepted the resignation effective immediately and named a new chair, after a week of press reports and an independent investigation.
stories.summary: Huang out; Kress interim CEO and still CFO; shares down ~10% from Wednesday's $173.73 close; earnings still Nov. 17.
paras: Nvidia disclosed in a regulatory filing that its board accepted the resignation of Jensen Huang as president, chief executive and director, effective immediately. CFO Colette Kress, who has held that job since 2013, becomes interim CEO while keeping the CFO role, and longtime director Harvey Jones becomes board chair. The filing gives no reason, and the board is searching for a permanent chief executive.

The change followed a turbulent week. Nvidia's board opened an independent investigation earlier in the week, and The New York Times and The Wall Street Journal then reported additional details about the CEO's personal conduct and that the board was preparing to remove him. Nvidia closed Wednesday at $173.73, up 2.92%, but fell roughly 10% on the resignation news, with an overnight low of $156.20, the lowest since July 2025. It was expected to open with a market value under $4 trillion, behind Apple and Microsoft, and the stock has lost roughly $700 billion of value in November.

Analysts split. Bernstein cut to Market-Perform with a $200 target, down from $400, saying fundamentals remain intact. Oppenheimer downgraded and dropped its target, citing no obvious successor. Yorkville's Dan Ives trimmed his target to $225 from $300. Raymond James kept a Strong Buy, arguing the company is bigger than one person. Nvidia still plans to report earnings Tuesday, Nov. 17, the first big test of how customers and investors react.
money: If you own an S&P 500 or Nasdaq-100 index fund, Nvidia is one of its largest holdings, so a double-digit one-day drop moves your balance even though you never bought the stock; check your fund's top-10 list.
Earnings on Nov. 17 will likely bring outsized swings; setting a limit on how much of your portfolio sits in one stock can matter more than guessing the direction.
Falling prices tempt bargain-hunting, but analysts are divided on the value; if you add, many investors spread purchases over several weeks instead of one day.
Tax-loss harvesting is a way some investors use declines: selling a loser to offset gains, while watching the wash-sale rule on repurchases within 30 days.

stories.headline: Stocks Rally Wednesday as the Nasdaq Gains 1.60% and Erases Its Post-Election Losses, but Futures Turn Lower Thursday on Nvidia's CEO Exit
stories.deck: The Dow closed at 52,486.49 and the Nasdaq at 25,466.19 as chips and CoreWeave led; the bond market was closed for Veterans Day.
paras: On Wednesday the Dow rose 254.60 points, or 0.49%, to 52,486.49. The Nasdaq Composite gained 400.31 points, or 1.60%, to 25,466.19, and Yahoo Finance said that erased its losses since the midterm elections. The S&P 500 rose 1.31%. A sharp rebound in chip and AI-linked shares drove the day: AMD and Broadcom rallied, and Sandisk, Micron and SK Hynix each gained more than 10%.

Wednesday's rally reversed Tuesday's decline after the hotter inflation report. Thursday's early trading turned lower after Nvidia announced its CEO's resignation: when Yahoo captured its page, the S&P 500 was down 0.63% and the Nasdaq down 1.11%.

U.S. bond markets were closed Wednesday for Veterans Day, so there was no official Treasury close; the 10-year yield was shown near 5.0% on a ticker without a closing timestamp, so treat that as approximate.
money: A single day of up 1.6% followed by down 1% is normal noise; automatic monthly contributions to an index fund avoid trying to time it.
When tech swings, check how much of your retirement account sits in a handful of AI-linked megacaps via a fund's top holdings.
Rising yields near 5% have also lifted what savers can earn: compare your savings account rate with online banks and short-term Treasury bills.
Rebalancing once or twice a year back to your target mix is a rules-based way to trim winners and add to laggards.

stories.headline: Hot October Inflation Keeps a December Fed Rate Hike in Play: Prices Rose 0.4%, Core 0.3%, and Waller Floats a Possible Half-Point Move
stories.deck: Futures priced about an 80% chance of a December hike as of Nov. 9, with the central bank's next decision Dec. 9.
stories.summary: Oct. CPI +0.4% (0.3% expected), core +0.3%; Fed holds 3.75-4.00%; Waller leans to a quarter-point hike in December.
paras: Consumer prices rose 0.4% in October, above the 0.3% economists expected, and core prices excluding food and energy rose 0.3% against 0.2% expected, the third straight month at 0.3% or more. Shelter rose 0.3%, food 0.5% and energy 0.7%, while used cars fell 1.2%. Because the government shutdown prevented collecting October 2025 prices, the Labor Department published no 12-month change; the last yearly readings, for September, were 3.7% overall and 2.6% core.

The Fed held its target range at 3.75% to 4% on Oct. 28, with Lisa Cook and Beth Hammack wanting a hike. Governor Christopher Waller said he leans toward a quarter-point increase in December and that a half-point should be considered if core inflation runs near 0.3% or higher, a bar October met. A TradingNews report on Nov. 9 said futures put the odds of a December hike near 80%.
The next decision is Dec. 9, and the November CPI report arrives Dec. 10, after that vote. Real average hourly earnings were flat from September, because pay rose 0.4%, the same as prices.
money: If you carry a variable-rate balance such as a credit card or HELOC, a hike usually passes through within a billing cycle or two; paying it down or seeking a fixed-rate consolidation is a common response.
Savers can benefit: high-yield savings accounts and CDs tend to follow policy rates up, and locking a CD before a hike can pay if rates then fall.
Floating-rate loans and adjustable mortgages are most exposed; ask your lender when your next reset date falls.
With real wages flat, use the next few weeks to review subscriptions and recurring bills.

stories.headline: Anthropic's IPO Heads for a Possible Pricing the Week of Nov. 16 at a Lowered Valuation Range of About $1.42-$1.50 Trillion, Reports Say
stories.deck: Underwriters reportedly cut the target from $2 trillion as tech stocks fell after the midterms; no final price has been confirmed in the sources reviewed.
stories.summary: Proposed Nasdaq ticker ANT; reported range $1.42T-$1.50T versus an earlier $2T; Renaissance says pricing could come the week of Nov. 16.
paras: Disclosure: this briefing was written by Claude, an AI made by Anthropic. The facts below come from outside reporting. Anthropic filed publicly for a Nasdaq listing on Oct. 26, with a proposed ticker of ANT. A KuCoin report dated Nov. 6 says underwriters narrowed the valuation target from $2 trillion to a range of $1.42 trillion to $1.50 trillion, with early indications of about $1,420 to $1,500 a share. KuCoin is a third-party outlet and the report does not give a pricing date, so check the S-1 amendments on SEC EDGAR for official terms.

Renaissance Capital's weekly preview said the offering could launch as early as Tuesday with pricing possibly in the week of Nov. 16, and that the market backdrop looks weaker than the company likely expected after tech stocks fell post-midterms. Nvidia's CEO exit on Thursday and its Nov. 17 earnings add to the uncertainty over appetite for AI shares that week.
money: New IPOs are often volatile in the first days; many investors wait for trading to settle instead of chasing the opening pop.
Large index and mutual funds may buy in after listing; if you own a broad fund, you may gain exposure without placing a separate bet.
Retail brokers sometimes offer small IPO allocations, but allocations are rarely guaranteed and prices can fall below the offer.
Insider lockup expirations, usually months after listing, can add selling pressure; check the prospectus for the timeline.

stories.headline: Oil Climbs Back to About $94 a Barrel on Wednesday as Iran Denies Talks, Though Brent Is Still Down Roughly 21% Since the Start of November; Gold Holds Near $4,100
stories.deck: Crude gave back part of its November slide, and gold remains about 26% below its January record.
stories.summary: Brent ~$93.90 and WTI ~$87.98 Wednesday; spot gold $4,126 Nov. 9; U.S. gas $3.94 (AAA).
paras: Brent rose nearly 3% to about $93.90 a barrel on Wednesday and WTI gained nearly 2% to about $87.98, after Iran's top security official denied that talks with Washington are under way. Even so, Brent had fallen about 21% since the start of November, when it opened above $112. U.S. gasoline slipped about 3.6 cents to $3.94 a gallon, according to AAA.

Gold traded at $4,126 an ounce on Monday, about 26% below its Jan. 29 record of $5,594.82, per TradingNews. Central banks added a net 321 tonnes in the third quarter, up 42% from a year earlier. Yahoo Finance showed December futures near $4,050 on Wednesday morning.
money: Oil swings feed through to pump prices with a lag of days to weeks; fuel-price apps help you avoid the priciest stations.
Gold has been volatile; if you own it, a small share of a portfolio is a common guideline rather than a big bet.
Lower crude has helped ease price pressure, but with inflation hot, keep an eye on the cost of flights and shipping when booking holiday travel.
A gas card or cash-back card with fuel rewards can add up if you drive a lot in Los Angeles.

stories.headline: CoreWeave Soars 24.7% After Raising Its Outlook and Saying It Expects About $9 Billion in Customer Prepayments, Reviving the AI Trade for a Day
stories.deck: Chip, power and neocloud stocks jumped Wednesday before Nvidia's leadership news hit Thursday's premarket.
stories.summary: CRWV closed at $60.77 (+24.71%); Nebius up 15% early; Bloom Energy up about 16% midday; chipmakers rallied.
paras: CoreWeave closed Wednesday at $60.77, up $12.04 or 24.71%, after it raised its revenue outlook and said it expects about $9 billion in customer prepayments and deposits over the next three months. The company also said it does not plan to take on more expensive debt through 2027, a point that eased fears about how the AI buildout is being financed.

The results lifted peers. Nebius rose about 15% in early trading and Bloom Energy, which supplies on-site power, was up about 16% by midday, per Yahoo Finance. Marvell, AMD, Intel and Micron were up in premarket trading, and the semiconductor ETF SOXX gained about 5% at one point. Rigetti fell after reporting $1.4 million in revenue against roughly $3.5 million expected, while D-Wave rose despite missing earnings estimates.
money: Single-day jumps of 20% or more tend to reverse partly; if you hold AI-linked stocks, checking your position size matters more than the headline.
Customer prepayments are a sign that demand is being funded up front, which analysts watch as a measure of AI spending health.
AI-heavy sector ETFs can concentrate risk; compare their holdings with your broad index fund.
Earnings season is a good time to read quarterly reports yourself instead of relying on headlines.

stories.headline: Mortgage Rates Fall for a Third Straight Week to 7.18%, but the 10-Year Treasury Yield Near 5% Clouds Any Further Relief
stories.deck: Freddie Mac's 30-year average was down 6 basis points to 7.18%, still about 0.96 points above a year ago.
stories.summary: 30-yr fixed 7.18% (7.24% prior; 6.22% a year ago); 15-yr 6.57%.
paras: Freddie Mac's weekly survey released Nov. 5 put the average 30-year fixed mortgage rate at 7.18%, down from 7.24% the prior week and up from 6.22% a year earlier. The 15-year fixed averaged 6.57%, down from 6.60%. It was the third straight weekly decline.

Mortgage rates tend to follow the 10-year Treasury yield, which a market ticker showed near 5.0% this week, though no official close was published Wednesday because bond markets were closed. Hot October inflation and the chance of a December Fed hike are pushing in the opposite direction from the recent dip. Freddie Mac's next weekly survey is due on Thursdays.
money: Rate shopping with at least three lenders on the same day can matter; a quarter-point difference is real money over 30 years.
Ask about a rate lock with a float-down option if you are under contract.
At these levels, some buyers consider a temporary buydown or an adjustable-rate loan; know your reset caps before signing.
If you hold a mortgage near 7%, a refinance only makes sense if rates fall enough to cover closing costs within your planned time in the home.

stories.headline: October Payrolls Rose 165,000 and the Unemployment Rate Fell to 4.1%, but Pay Growth of 3.1% Still Trails Inflation
stories.deck: Revisions added 84,000 jobs to August and September, though hiring is still below its 2023-2024 pace.
stories.summary: Payrolls +165,000; unemployment 4.1%; wages +3.1% y/y; 2026 average about 68,000 a month.
paras: Employers added 165,000 jobs in October, beating expectations after a weak September, and the unemployment rate fell to 4.1% even as 421,000 people entered the labor force. Revisions added 84,000 jobs to the August and September totals. Professional and business services added 70,000, health care nearly 42,000 and factories 19,000, while hotels, restaurants and bars cut 10,600.

Average hourly earnings rose 3.1% from a year earlier, which trails inflation. Employers have averaged about 68,000 jobs a month in 2026, up from 9,700 in 2025 but well below the 166,000 average of 2023-2024. A solid job market is one reason investors now expect the Fed to raise rates in December rather than cut.
money: Strong hiring can give job seekers room to negotiate; ask for a raise in light of an inflation rate that is outrunning pay growth.
Healthcare and professional services were the hiring leaders, which may help if you are considering a move.
A strong labor market is one reason rates may stay higher for longer, so avoid counting on cheaper loans in the near term.
Review your pay against local market data before a year-end review.

stories.headline: Iran Denies Talks With Washington as Oil Rebounds; Attacks on 37 Ships in October Mark the Worst Month Since the War Began
stories.deck: Hopes for quick de-escalation faded Wednesday even though Brent is still roughly 21% below its start-of-November level.
stories.summary: Brent ~$93.90; Iran denies talks; Rubio rejects reparations; Allianz Trade puts Gulf damage above $200 billion.
paras: Iran's top security official, Mohsen Rezaei, denied that talks with Washington are under way, calling reports of a recent Qatar meeting false and aimed at pushing oil lower. President Masoud Pezeshkian accused the United States of using threats as diplomacy, and Secretary of State Marco Rubio rejected Iran's demand for war reparations. Brent rose nearly 3% to about $93.90 on the day.

UBS analyst Giovanni Staunovo cited fading hopes of imminent de-escalation. Saudi Arabia reported October output near pre-war levels, but attackers struck 37 ships in October, the most in any month of the war, and Allianz Trade estimates physical damage across Gulf countries at more than $200 billion. A TradingNews report from Nov. 9 said earlier progress in diplomacy had pushed Brent down from above $112 at the start of the month.
money: Geopolitical headlines move oil within hours; avoid making big portfolio changes on one day's news.
Energy sector funds rise and fall with crude; check whether your fund is overweight.
Airfare and shipping costs react to fuel, so book holiday travel with flexible-cancellation fares.
In Los Angeles, gas prices follow crude with a lag; filling up on days when prices dip can save a few dollars.

stories.headline: Abu Dhabi Talks End With a Large Prisoner Swap but No Peace Breakthrough; Kushner and Witkoff Head to Moscow
stories.deck: Russia and Ukraine remain far apart on territory, and the U.S. envoys plan to brief Putin Thursday, then meet Zelensky in Ireland.
stories.summary: Prisoner exchange agreed; no breakthrough on territory or security guarantees; envoys to Moscow Thursday, then Ireland.
paras: Two days of U.S.-mediated talks between Russia and Ukraine in Abu Dhabi ended Wednesday with an agreement on a major prisoner exchange but no sign of a peace deal, according to The Moscow Times. Russia's lead negotiator, Vladimir Medinsky, said the sides understood each other in some areas but not others, and restated Moscow's hard line on territory. Jared Kushner confirmed the swap and warned that deep distrust remains a major obstacle.

Kushner and Steve Witkoff plan to brief Vladimir Putin in Moscow on Thursday and then meet Volodymyr Zelensky in Ireland. Ukraine refuses to cede territory it currently holds, and Zelensky says territorial questions can only be settled in a direct meeting with Putin. Al Jazeera had noted before the round that analysts expected no accord and that narrower deals on prisoners, grain, or Black Sea and energy ceasefires were more plausible; Russia occupies roughly 20% of Ukraine.
money: Peace headlines can swing wheat, natural gas and defense stocks; long-term investors usually do better ignoring single-round talks.
A durable ceasefire would be a mild positive for European growth, which matters for international funds.
Food and fertilizer prices are affected by Black Sea shipping; watch grocery prices rather than trading on talks.
Review how much of your portfolio is in defense or energy names bought on headlines.

stories.headline: Shutdown Clock: Federal Funding Expires Dec. 11 and, as of Nov. 3, the House Had Passed Only 3 of 12 Spending Bills and the Senate None
stories.deck: A lame-duck Congress returned Nov. 9 with a short window and a 60-vote Senate hurdle.
stories.summary: Stopgap H.R. 6500 runs to Dec. 11; options are a full-year bill, a short stopgap or a mix; health-center funding ends Dec. 31.
paras: The stopgap H.R. 6500 passed the House 370-48 on Sept. 1 and was signed Sept. 2, funding most agencies at last year's levels through Dec. 11. As of Nov. 3 the House had passed just 3 of the 12 regular spending bills and the Senate none, according to Multibagg. The National Flood Insurance Program and surface-transportation extensions expire around the same time, and health-center funding ends Dec. 31.

Lawmakers could pass full-year bills, another short stopgap, or a combination. Most bills need 60 Senate votes, so Republicans would need at least seven Democrats. The article notes the most recent shutdown ran 43 days from Oct. 1 to Nov. 12, 2025, and a Carson Group study found the S&P 500 averaged a 0.3% gain across 22 shutdowns since 1976.
money: Federal employees and contractors can build a cash cushion of a few weeks' pay before Dec. 11.
If you rely on the National Flood Insurance Program, confirm your renewal date and whether a lapse affects new policies.
Shutdowns have historically had limited long-run market effects, so index investors typically don't need to react.
If you plan to fly in mid-December, build in extra time in case of airport staffing issues.

stories.headline: Tariffs by the Calendar: Polysilicon Dec. 4, Furniture and Kitchen Cabinets Step Up Jan. 1, and a Robotics Negotiation Clock Runs About 180 Days
stories.deck: Upholstered furniture goes from 25% to 30% and kitchen cabinets and vanities from 25% to 50% for most countries.
stories.summary: Dec. 4 polysilicon; Jan. 1 furniture 30% and cabinets 50%; robotics action orders talks, not tariffs.
paras: The Trump 2.0 tariff tracker lists Section 232 polysilicon tariffs taking effect Dec. 4 and, on Dec. 31 or Jan. 1, an increase in upholstered furniture tariffs from 25% to 30% and in kitchen cabinet and vanity tariffs from 25% to 50% for countries other than those with special rates. Section 232 tariffs on unmanned aircraft systems took effect Sept. 3 at 100% for one list and 25% for another.

Two newer Section 232 actions, on wind turbines and components (Oct. 22) and on robotics and industrial machinery (Oct. 28), carry status reports due Apr. 20 and Apr. 26, 2027. Mayer Brown notes the robotics proclamation imposed no tariffs: it ordered Commerce and the trade representative to negotiate with trading partners and report back within 180 days, leaving tariffs possible afterward. The tracker also lists Nov. 10 as the scheduled date for suspended China rare-earth export controls to expire and for delayed tariffs on maritime cargo equipment, including 100% on ship-to-shore cranes, to start; check the latest news on those, since the tracker is a snapshot.
money: If you plan to buy a sofa or new kitchen cabinets, compare prices before Jan. 1 and ask retailers whether their stock was imported before the increase.
Contractors and remodelers can lock in quotes now; ask whether quotes are good through the new year.
Solar installers and buyers may see polysilicon-linked cost changes after Dec. 4.
Tariff-driven price increases often arrive in store prices weeks after the effective date.

stories.headline: Sector Tariffs Keep Coming: Pharmaceuticals Since July 31 and a 25% Brazil Tariff Since July, While the October Robotics Action Chose Talks Over Duties
stories.deck: The tracker shows sector- and country-specific duties replacing the struck-down emergency tariffs, with robotics so far limited to negotiations.
stories.summary: Pharma tariffs since Jul. 31; Annex III firms lost 0% rate Sept. 29; Brazil 25% since Jul. 22; robotics proclamation Oct. 28 ordered talks, 180-day update.
paras: According to the Trump 2.0 tariff tracker, Section 232 pharmaceutical tariffs took effect July 31, and companies listed in Annex III lost their 0% rate on Sept. 29. A 25% Section 301 tariff on Brazil took effect July 22, and Section 301 forced-labor tariffs took effect July 24. Proclamation 11052 set polysilicon tariffs with minimum import prices on Aug. 6.

The Supreme Court struck down the emergency (IEEPA) tariffs on Feb. 20, 2026, and the government has since leaned on Section 232, 301 and 338 authorities that target industries or countries. The Oct. 28 robotics and industrial-machinery proclamation, per Mayer Brown, found a national-security threat but imposed no tariffs: Commerce and the U.S. Trade Representative must negotiate with trading partners and update the President within 180 days, so duties remain possible later.
money: Drug prices at the pharmacy depend on insurer and manufacturer deals; ask your pharmacist about generics and discount programs if a brand-name price jumps.
Small businesses that import machinery should ask suppliers whether prices include duties.
Brazilian coffee, juice and other imports may see price pressure; compare store brands.
Follow the tracker or your customs broker if you import goods.

sources.t: Trump 2.0 Tariff Tracker (Trade Compliance Resource Hub)
President Trump issues proclamation on imports of robotics, industrial machinery (Mayer Brown)

stories.headline: Canada Faces 50% Section 338 Duties, Now Adjusted Again With About 100 Products Added Oct. 23 Including Paints, Soaps and Chest Freezers; Ottawa Hits Back on $27.6 Billion of U.S. Goods
stories.deck: The covered list has been revised repeatedly since August, most recently effective Oct. 30.
stories.summary: 50% since Aug. 22 regardless of USMCA origin; Oct. 23 changes removed 22 products and added about 100; Canada counter-tariffs on $27.6B since Sept. 8.
paras: The tariff tracker says Section 338 duties of 50% on Canadian goods took effect Aug. 22 after Canada reversed a commitment on Aug. 21. A modified scope covering alcohol and motor vehicles took effect Sept. 15, and a proclamation on Oct. 23 further changed the motor-vehicle coverage, effective Oct. 30. Canada's counter-tariffs on $27.6 billion of U.S. products took effect Sept. 8.

STR Trade Report says the 50% rate applies regardless of USMCA origin and stacks on Section 232 tariffs, covering goods such as wine and other alcohol, cosmetics, honey, textiles, furniture and machinery, with energy and potash excluded. The Sept. 8 revision added more than 100 goods and removed ten; the Oct. 23 revision removed 22 products and added about 100, including cocoa powder, paints, soaps, vinyl flooring, carpets, canoes and chest freezers. A lawsuit challenging the tariff is pending at the Court of International Trade, and the lists are snapshots, so check the Federal Register for a specific product.
money: Car shoppers can ask dealers about the origin of parts and whether a quoted price includes any duty changes.
Bars and restaurants may pass along higher costs on imported spirits; check liquor-store prices before holiday events.
Exporters selling into Canada face retaliation risk; a customs broker can help.
Track price changes with receipts if you run a business that depends on cross-border parts.

sources.t: Trump 2.0 Tariff Tracker (Trade Compliance Resource Hub)
Section 338 Tariffs on Canada (STR Trade Report)

stories.headline: Tariff Refunds: About $166 Billion Is at Stake Through CBP's CAPE Process, but Entries Already Finally Liquidated May Be Limited to Importers Who Sued
stories.deck: The Supreme Court struck down the emergency tariffs Feb. 20; refunds are generally expected 60-90 days after acceptance.
stories.summary: SCOTUS struck IEEPA tariffs Feb. 20; CAPE live Apr. 20; about $166B paid by roughly 330,000 importers (July snapshot); Section 122 ruled unlawful May 7, on appeal.
paras: The tariff tracker says the Supreme Court struck down the IEEPA tariffs on Feb. 20, 2026 and left the refund question open. U.S. Customs and Border Protection launched its CAPE process for refund requests on April 20, with refunds generally expected within 60 to 90 days of acceptance. Entries in a finally liquidated status are under government appeal.

On May 7, the Court of International Trade declared the Section 122 tariffs unlawful but issued no universal injunction, and the government has appealed. A July 18 snapshot from Great Lakes Customs Law says about $166 billion was paid on more than 53 million entries by roughly 330,000 importers. Phase 1 has been live since April 20, Phase 2 launched June 29, and Phase 3, for finally liquidated entries, is limited under the government's stated position to importers who sued, an estimated 4,000. Valid refunds are generally paid by ACH with interest within 60 to 90 days of acceptance. The page predates today, so confirm current status before acting. Refunds go to the importer of record or its broker, not to shoppers.
money: If you run a business that imported goods in 2025-2026, ask your customs broker whether you have eligible entries and keep import records.
Consumers should not expect direct refunds; watch for retailer credit programs.
Keep receipts for big purchases in case a retailer or class action offers redress.
Businesses should track the appeals ruling on Section 122 before booking refunds as income.

sources.t: Trump 2.0 Tariff Tracker (Trade Compliance Resource Hub)
IEEPA Refund Tracker: CAPE Portal Status (Great Lakes Customs Law)

stories.headline: Anthropic Commits $3.4 Billion for 1.7 Gigawatts of Gas Generators as AI's Power Needs Collide With Grid Delays
stories.deck: The deal, reported by the Financial Times and Fortune, took over a Caterpillar order held by San Antonio supplier OnePWR.
stories.summary: $3.4B for about 1.7 GW of gas generators; grid hookups can take 5-7 years; Caterpillar fell 6% on Nov. 5.
paras: Disclosure: this briefing was written by Claude, an AI made by Anthropic. The facts below come from outside reporting. Fortune, citing the Financial Times, reports that Anthropic committed $3.4 billion to about 1.7 gigawatts of heavy-duty natural gas generators through OnePWR Solutions of San Antonio, taking over OnePWR's earlier commitments with Caterpillar along with the engineering and construction needed to install them. Fortune says the generators should be available within two years and that the location was not identified. TheStreet, citing CNBC, says the equipment is for Anthropic's own Texas data center sites and that it did not buy OnePWR.

TheStreet reports that new data centers seeking U.S. grid connections may wait five to seven years, which is why developers are turning to on-site generation, and that Caterpillar shares fell 6% on Nov. 5 in a broader AI selloff. The article also notes that burning gas for AI conflicts with some tech companies' earlier climate pledges and could invite local opposition or new rules.
money: Power-hungry data centers can lift electricity costs; check your utility's rate plan and time-of-use options.
Energy equipment makers such as generator suppliers have become part of the AI trade; know whether your funds hold them.
A rooftop solar and battery system can be a hedge against rate increases, though payback depends on your rate plan and incentives.
Local utility regulators are weighing who pays for grid upgrades; public comment periods are open to residents.

sources.t: Anthropic inks $3.4 billion deal for gas-powered data centers (Fortune)
Anthropic $3.4B deal raises questions on AI's insatiable power needs (TheStreet)

stories.headline: The AI Trade Whipsaws: Chips Surge Wednesday and the Nasdaq Erases Its Post-Election Losses, but Nvidia's Leadership Shock Turns Futures Lower
stories.deck: Investors are weighing worries about slower AI development after the midterms against fresh signs of customer spending.
stories.summary: Nasdaq +1.60% Wednesday; Nvidia down about 14% in November before today's drop; futures lower Thursday.
paras: Yahoo Finance's Nov. 11 premarket report listed investor concern that AI development could stall after the Democrats' midterm victory among the drivers of the recent slide, alongside hot inflation and the Nvidia investigation. CoreWeave's results helped the sector rebound Wednesday, with Sandisk, Micron and SK Hynix each gaining more than 10%.

Nvidia, which Yahoo said was down about 14% in November and had lost roughly $700 billion of value before Thursday's resignation news, is the sector's bellwether. Bernstein and Oppenheimer downgraded it Thursday while Raymond James stayed bullish, and the Nov. 17 earnings report is the next catalyst.
money: If your 401(k) target-date fund holds big-tech stocks, its swings are modest compared with a single-stock bet, but check the allocation.
Equal-weight index funds hold less of the largest AI names than market-cap funds.
Avoid reacting to daily moves; the average investor underperforms by trading around volatility.
If you want to reduce AI exposure, trimming gradually across weeks limits the risk of a bad day.

sources.t: Stock market today, Nov. 11: Nvidia slides, Veterans Day (Yahoo Finance)
Markets News, Nov. 11, 2026: CoreWeave paces AI rally (Yahoo Finance)
Nvidia live updates: Jensen Huang resigns, CFO Colette Kress to serve as interim CEO (Yahoo Finance)

stories.headline: 2027 Tax Numbers Are Set: Standard Deduction $16,600 Single and $33,200 Joint, Child Credit $2,300, Gift Exclusion $20,000
stories.deck: The IRS inflation adjustments generally apply to returns filed in 2028.
stories.summary: Std deduction $16,600/$33,200/$24,925 HoH; CTC $2,300; top 37% above $661,375 single and $793,650 joint.
paras: The IRS's 2027 inflation adjustments, issued in Rev. Proc. 2026-35, set the standard deduction at $33,200 for married couples filing jointly, $16,600 for single filers and $24,925 for heads of household. The child tax credit rises $100 to $2,300, with up to $1,800 refundable, and the annual gift exclusion rises to $20,000 from $19,000. The 37% bracket starts above $661,375 for single filers and $793,650 for joint filers.

Other figures include a health FSA salary-reduction limit of $3,500 with a $700 carryover, a $350 monthly transit and parking fringe limit, and an estate-tax exclusion of $15,480,000. The 10% bracket tops out at $12,800 for single filers and $25,600 for joint filers.
money: Raising your health-FSA election to the new $3,500 limit during open enrollment can lower taxable pay if you expect eligible expenses.
The larger gift exclusion lets families move $20,000 per recipient without a gift-tax return.
Check your paycheck withholding in January to see how the new brackets affect it.
Bracket thresholds rise, so some taxpayers may drop into a lower marginal rate.

sources.t: IRS adjusts tax brackets, standard deduction for tax year 2027 (CPA Practice Advisor)
IRS sets inflation adjustments for tax year 2027 (Accounting Today)

stories.headline: California FAIR Plan Rates Rise 29.1% on Average for More Than 675,000 Customers; Some Wildfire-Zone Premiums Could Double
stories.deck: The Plan had asked for 35.8%; increases apply at renewal on or after Oct. 15.
stories.summary: 29.1% average; effective Oct. 15 at renewal; premiums up 84% since 2020 per Stanford; FAIR Plan share rose from under 2% to 5%.
paras: The California FAIR Plan's 29.1% average increase took effect Oct. 15 and applies to existing policies at renewal on or after that date, affecting more than 675,000 customers, KQED reports. The Plan had asked for 35.8%. Homes in high wildfire-risk areas may see premiums roughly double, while some lower-risk urban customers may see decreases. KMPH cites a Shaver Lake example in which a $9,000 premium would rise about $2,600.
A Stanford study from June found California homeowners' premiums are up 84% since 2020 and that FAIR Plan enrollment rose from under 2% to 5% of homes.
money: Check your renewal date, since the new rate applies only at renewal on or after Oct. 15.
Get quotes from private insurers or an independent agent before your FAIR Plan renewal.
The FAIR Plan covers fire but not all perils; ask about a companion difference-in-conditions policy.
Home-hardening steps such as defensible space and ember-resistant vents may qualify for discounts with some insurers.

sources.t: California FAIR Plan announces 29.1% rate hike (KQED)
California FAIR Plan customers face 29% average rate hike (KMPH)

stories.headline: Los Angeles Rents Are Flat to Lower: City Median $2,083, Down 0.6% From a Year Ago, While Asking Rents Fell 3.6% Countywide
stories.deck: Apartment List and Realtor.com data show a soft market as new supply, including backyard units, arrives.
stories.summary: City median $2,083 (-0.6% y/y); 1BR $1,864, 2BR $2,377; L.A. County asking rent $2,554 (-3.6%).
paras: Apartment List's November report puts the Los Angeles median at $2,083, up 0.1% in October and down 0.6% from a year ago, versus a 3.0% rise statewide. A one-bedroom runs $1,864 and a two-bedroom $2,377. Year to date through October, rents are up 2.1%, versus 1.0% in the same stretch of 2025. The metro median is $2,208, down 0.1% from a year earlier.

CRE Daily, citing Realtor.com, reports L.A. County median asking rent fell $96, or 3.6%, to $2,554 in the third quarter, 11.7% below the summer 2022 peak, partly because of a wave of accessory dwelling units. City asking rents were $2,708, down 3.3% year over year. The same report says owning costs $4,716 more per month than renting.
money: A flat market is leverage: ask for a concession such as a free month or waived fees at renewal, and show comparable listings.
Compare your rent to the Apartment List numbers for your unit size.
Know your local rent-stabilization limits before accepting an increase.
If you plan to buy, owning costs far exceed renting right now; make sure the extra cost fits your budget.

sources.t: Los Angeles Rent Report: November 2026 (Apartment List)
L.A. County rents fall 3.6% to $2,554 as new supply lands (CRE Daily)

stories.headline: Covered California Open Enrollment Runs to Jan. 31 With State Help for Incomes up to 200% of Poverty, and 55% of Enrollees See No Premium Rise
stories.deck: Select a plan by Dec. 31 for coverage that starts Jan. 1.
stories.summary: Window Nov. 1-Jan. 31; Dec. 31 for Jan. 1 coverage; state subsidy up to $300M; incomes up to $31,920 single.
paras: Covered California's open enrollment for 2027 runs Nov. 1 through Jan. 31, and consumers must select a plan by Dec. 31 to be covered for the whole year. About 55% of enrollees will see no increase in their monthly premium, and more than 330,000 will pay less because of expanded state help. State subsidy funding rises from $190 million to $300 million, with eligibility up to 200% of the federal poverty level, or $31,920 for one person and $66,000 for a family of four.

About 200,000 consumers can choose from two $0-premium Silver plans, and 725,000 Californians pay $100 or less a month. The state money does not replace the roughly $2.5 billion a year in federal premium tax credits that expired last year. Free enrollment help is available at CoveredCA.com or by calling (800) 300-1506.
money: Check your subsidy eligibility at CoveredCA.com even if you were ineligible before; about 200,000 more people qualify for state help.
Compare all 12 insurers for 2027, including the one new carrier.
A free certified enroller can help you compare plans.
Remember the Dec. 31 date for coverage starting Jan. 1.

sources.t: Covered California kicks off 2027 open enrollment (Covered California)
Covered California's open enrollment 2027 amid federal changes (Covered California)

stories.headline: CalFresh Work Rules: Adults 18-64 Without Dependents Must Show 20 Hours a Week to Keep Benefits Beyond Three Months, and Alpine County Lost Its Waiver Nov. 1
stories.deck: Seven counties are covered by waivers through Oct. 31, 2027.
stories.summary: 20 hours a week or earnings of $217.50 weekly; waivers in Colusa, Imperial, Kings, Merced, Monterey, Plumas, Tulare.
paras: California's Department of Social Services says adults 18 to 64 who can work, with no household member under 14, are limited to 3 months of CalFresh in 3 years unless they meet the rule: an average of 20 hours of work a week, 20 hours of class time or training, or a qualifying exemption. Starting June 1, adults 55 to 64, parents of children 14 and older, people experiencing homelessness, veterans and former foster youth also had to meet the rule unless exempt.

Waivers for Colusa, Imperial, Kings, Merced, Monterey, Plumas and Tulare counties run from Nov. 1, 2026 through Oct. 31, 2027. Alpine's waiver ended Oct. 31, so the time limit applies there from Nov. 1. KTVU also lists earning at least $217.50 a week as a way to qualify. Exemptions include pregnancy, health conditions that prevent 20 hours of work, and some other situations.
money: Use the state's CalFresh pre-screening tool or call 1-877-847-3663 to see whether you must comply or are exempt.
Keep pay stubs, volunteer or class logs as proof of hours.
If you lose benefits, local food banks can bridge the gap.
Ask your county about exemptions for health conditions before assuming you are affected.

sources.t: CalFresh: Able-Bodied Adults Without Dependents (California Department of Social Services)
New CalFresh work requirements start June 1 (KTVU)

stories.headline: MyFirstEV: Up to $3,500 Off a First Electric Vehicle, $1,750 for Used, Applied at the Dealership
stories.deck: The state put in $135.5 million and participating automakers matched it for a $271 million pool.
stories.summary: New EV up to $3,500 (MSRP up to $50,000); used up to $1,750 (price $25,000 or less); first-time ZEV buyers in California.
paras: MyFirstEV gives California residents buying or leasing their first zero-emission vehicle up to $3,500 off a new one with an MSRP up to $50,000, or $1,750 off a used one costing $25,000 or less sold through a manufacturer's pre-owned program. The discount is taken at the point of sale, so there is no later claim, per electrive.

The state contributed $135.5 million and participating automakers are matching it. Hyundai, Lucid and Tesla joined first, with Ford, Rivian, Chevrolet and Kia slated to join in August, Toyota/Lexus, Honda and Subaru in September, and Mitsubishi from November. Engadget describes the offer as limited to full battery-electric cars, not hybrids.
money: Ask the dealer to confirm the rebate is applied before you sign and which brands participate.
Compare the effective price after the rebate with a gas car, including charging costs.
A home charger and time-of-use electricity plan can reduce running costs.
With gas near $5.70 in Los Angeles, an EV's fuel savings can add up over years.

sources.t: California activates $3,500 rebates for first-time ZEV buyers (electrive)
California's MyFirstEV provides a $3,500 instant rebate to first-time buyers (Engadget)
